title: The band he would form and playing lead
summary: Albert says he would rebuild his 1929-32 band if he could find such loyal men, and talks about glasses and playing first trumpet.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Well, if you could organize a band now, get anybody who wanted to, who would play these? Who would you hire a band?

If I could organize a band again, and I could organize a band like the Don Albert Band from the year of 1929 to say 1932, and I could get individuals that was in that band, yes, I would organize a band tomorrow. And I'm not going to find them. I'm not going to find them. You have to face backs. Those were loyal musicians. They treated each other as though they were brothers. Even old man Johnson, as old as he was, he considered himself one of us. Yes, I'd organize a band, but you can't find them. So then you just resolve through the situation as it is, let the world go like it's going on, and you just try to play your part.
Well, I find that so many musicians want to play the lead, man. That's all I do. They're on that mind. It doesn't matter what instrument they play, they want to be strong.
You don't mean play a lead. They want to be the leaders.
Right. Well, yeah, and try to play a lead on drums if you don't want to. Right.

If he's going to try to out- You can't play a lead. Right. But he still wants to be that lead. Well, I would want to play the first trumpet again. And now there again, my sight would prevent me from reading the notes as I should. It's hard to read with glasses on because you'll affect your voice. I never thought of that. Well, yeah, sometimes your glasses slip down off your face, you have to stop to raise it back up and do different things. And then it's with the, with, over your ear. It has a lot of disadvantages, a lot of disadvantages.
Yeah, you don't see many guys sitting on his tracks with glasses.
